description: FX regime analytics over the shared `dropset` database: the basis against an FX anchor in bps, and how a product's volatility varies by weekend, trading session, and hour of day. Sibling to the Market-data dashboard, which answers whether ingestion is alive; this one answers what the data says. The deviation panels need an FX anchor source and stay empty until one is collected — every other panel is single-leg and works today.

panels.description: The basis, made visible. Venue price divided by its FX anchor, in basis points: POSITIVE means the venue product trades RICH to the interbank rate, NEGATIVE means cheap. Both legs must be quoted the same way round for the ratio to mean anything — a venue symbol quoted inverted produces a wrong series rather than an obviously broken one, so check the quote direction before trusting a reading. The two legs are aligned onto a common grid rather than joined on the raw bucket, because the collectors do not all run at one granularity and an equi-join would silently return nothing. Set the alignment to the coarser of the two feeds. Empty until an FX anchor source is collected.

targets.rawSql:
WITH venue AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (bucket_start / $align_secs)
         (bucket_start / $align_secs) * $align_secs AS aligned_start,
         close AS venue_close
  FROM cex_prices
  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
    AND source = '$venue_source'
    AND product_id = '$venue_product'
  ORDER BY bucket_start / $align_secs, bucket_start DESC
),
anchor AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (bucket_start / $align_secs)
         (bucket_start / $align_secs) * $align_secs AS aligned_start,
         close AS anchor_close
  FROM cex_prices
  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
    AND source = '$anchor_source'
    AND product_id = '$anchor_product'
  ORDER BY bucket_start / $align_secs, bucket_start DESC
)
SELECT
  to_timestamp(v.aligned_start) AS "time",
  '$venue_product vs $anchor_product' AS metric,
  (v.venue_close / a.anchor_close - 1) * 10000 AS value
FROM venue v
JOIN anchor a USING (aligned_start)
WHERE a.anchor_close > 0
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Deviation from FX anchor (bps)

panels.description: The latest aligned basis reading, in bps. Thresholds are deliberately wide and are a legibility aid rather than a risk limit — what counts as a large deviation depends entirely on the pair and on whether interbank FX is currently open, since with the FX market shut there is no arbitrage channel and the basis is free to widen.

WITH venue AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (bucket_start / $align_secs)

anchor AS (

  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)

panels.title: Current basis

panels.description: Per-bar realized volatility in bps, by hour of day, split into weekday and weekend. This is the vol-ladder's sigma input. Returns are computed between genuinely ADJACENT buckets only: a venue emits no candle for a minute with no trades, and interbank FX leaves a ~48-hour hole every weekend, so a plain window function would bridge those gaps and dump one enormous pseudo-return into a single hour — which reads exactly like a real time-of-day effect. Read the bar counts on the summary table below before trusting a thin cell; on a sparse book these cells fall to single digits, where a standard deviation is arithmetic rather than information.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bars AS (
  SELECT bucket_start, close
  FROM cex_prices
  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
    AND source = '$venue_source'
    AND product_id = '$venue_product'
    AND granularity_secs = $granularity
),
returns AS (
  SELECT
    to_timestamp(bucket_start) AS bucket_ts,
    CASE
      WHEN lag(bucket_start) OVER w = bucket_start - $granularity
           AND lag(close) OVER w > 0
           AND close > 0
      THEN ln(close / lag(close) OVER w)
    END AS r
  FROM bars
  WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY bucket_start)
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE '$hour_tz')::int AS hour_of_day,
    CASE
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 6
        THEN 'weekend'
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 0
           AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') < 17
        THEN 'weekend'
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 5
           AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') >= 17
        THEN 'weekend'
      ELSE 'weekday'
    END AS regime,
    r
  FROM returns
)
SELECT
  hour_of_day,
  stddev_samp(r) FILTER (WHERE regime = 'weekday') * 10000 AS weekday,
  stddev_samp(r) FILTER (WHERE regime = 'weekend') * 10000 AS weekend
FROM classified
GROUP BY hour_of_day
ORDER BY hour_of_day

panels.title: Realized vol by hour ($hour_tz)

panels.description: Per-bar realized volatility in bps, by FX trading session. Answers whether an FX stablecoin inherits the rhythm of its underlying currency's home session or trades on crypto's own flat 24/7 clock. Sessions are local wall-clock windows in each centre — Sydney and Tokyo 08:00/09:00 local, London and New York 08:00 local — resolved per timestamp, so daylight saving is handled rather than approximated; the northern and southern hemispheres shift in opposite directions, which no fixed UTC range can express. Sessions OVERLAP and a bar is counted in each it falls in, so the counts sum to more than the total. That is deliberate: the London/New York overlap is the highest-liquidity window of the FX day and collapsing it into an exclusive bucket would hide the effect being measured. Compare sessions to each other; do not add them up.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bars AS (
  SELECT bucket_start, close
  FROM cex_prices
  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
    AND source = '$venue_source'
    AND product_id = '$venue_product'
    AND granularity_secs = $granularity
),
returns AS (
  SELECT
    to_timestamp(bucket_start) AS bucket_ts,
    CASE
      WHEN lag(bucket_start) OVER w = bucket_start - $granularity
           AND lag(close) OVER w > 0
           AND close > 0
      THEN ln(close / lag(close) OVER w)
    END AS r
  FROM bars
  WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY bucket_start)
),
sessions (session, tz, open_hour, close_hour) AS (
  VALUES
    ('1 Sydney',   'Australia/Sydney', 8, 17),
    ('2 Tokyo',    'Asia/Tokyo',       9, 18),
    ('3 London',   'Europe/London',    8, 17),
    ('4 New York', 'America/New_York', 8, 17)
)
SELECT
  s.session,
  stddev_samp(r.r) * 10000 AS vol_bps_per_bar
FROM returns r
JOIN sessions s
  ON EXTRACT(HOUR FROM r.bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE s.tz) >= s.open_hour
 AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM r.bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE s.tz) < s.close_hour
 AND EXTRACT(DOW FROM r.bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE s.tz) BETWEEN 1 AND 5
GROUP BY s.session
ORDER BY s.session

panels.title: Realized vol by FX session

panels.description: Weekend against weekday for the selected product, with the tape-quality columns beside the volatility figure. The FX week runs Sunday 17:00 to Friday 17:00 New York time, expressed in that city's local clock so the boundary stays correct across daylight saving. `bars` is the column to read first: it is what tells you whether a volatility number below it is measurement or arithmetic. `distinct_closes` is texture, NOT a fabrication detector — a genuinely traded weekend carries very few distinct prices, and on this repo's own data weekends show MORE distinct closes per bar than weekdays, so any rule keyed on that ratio fires on honest data.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bars AS (
  SELECT bucket_start, close, high, low
  FROM cex_prices
  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
    AND source = '$venue_source'
    AND product_id = '$venue_product'
    AND granularity_secs = $granularity
),
regimes AS (
  SELECT
    bucket_start,
    close,
    high,
    low,
    to_timestamp(bucket_start) AS bucket_ts,
    CASE
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM to_timestamp(bucket_start) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 6
        THEN 'weekend'
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM to_timestamp(bucket_start) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 0
           AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM to_timestamp(bucket_start) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') < 17
        THEN 'weekend'
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM to_timestamp(bucket_start) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 5
           AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM to_timestamp(bucket_start) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') >= 17
        THEN 'weekend'
      ELSE 'weekday'
    END AS regime
  FROM bars
),
returns AS (
  SELECT
    regime,
    close,
    high,
    low,
    CASE
      WHEN lag(bucket_start) OVER w = bucket_start - $granularity
           AND lag(close) OVER w > 0
           AND close > 0
      THEN ln(close / lag(close) OVER w)
    END AS r
  FROM regimes
  WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY bucket_start)
)
SELECT
  regime,
  count(*) AS bars,
  count(r) AS return_pairs,
  stddev_samp(r) * 10000 AS vol_bps_per_bar,
  avg(abs(r)) * 10000 AS mean_abs_move_bps,
  max(abs(r)) * 10000 AS max_abs_move_bps,
  count(DISTINCT close) AS distinct_closes,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE high = low) AS zero_range_bars
FROM returns
GROUP BY regime
ORDER BY regime

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT source FROM cex_prices ORDER BY 1
list.description: The venue leg: whose candles are being analyzed. Single-select, because every panel here measures one product's behavior rather than comparing venues.
list.label: Venue source
list.name: venue_source
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT source FROM cex_prices ORDER BY 1

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM cex_prices WHERE source = '$venue_source' ORDER BY 1
list.description: The product to analyze, listing only what the selected venue actually carries. The filter on the source is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: an unfiltered list offers every product any source has ever written, so it invites pairing a venue with a symbol it does not and could not quote. The committed default is the product with a genuinely traded tape — a sparse book yields per-hour cells too thin to compute a standard deviation over, so start here and re-point deliberately.
list.label: Venue product
list.name: venue_product
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM cex_prices WHERE source = '$venue_source' ORDER BY 1

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT source FROM cex_prices ORDER BY 1
list.description: The FX anchor leg's source. Prefer a source that publishes NO bars while interbank FX is closed: the deviation series stays honest either way, but a source that keeps printing through a shut market makes any weekend volatility figure meaningless.
list.label: Anchor source
list.name: anchor_source
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT source FROM cex_prices ORDER BY 1

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM cex_prices WHERE source = '$anchor_source' ORDER BY 1
list.description: The FX anchor pair, canonical uppercase ISO-4217 base-quote, listing only what the selected anchor source actually publishes. Two constraints this picker does NOT enforce, and which are on you: the anchor must be quoted the same way round as the venue product, and it must be the SAME currency family — pairing a venue product against an unrelated currency's rate yields a large, stable, entirely meaningless number rather than an obvious error. Tagging products by currency family so the pairing can be checked rather than trusted is tracked separately.
list.label: Anchor product
list.name: anchor_product
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM cex_prices WHERE source = '$anchor_source' ORDER BY 1

list.description: Bucket size of the single-leg panels, in seconds. A fixed list rather than a query on the data, so it is never empty on a cold database. 60 is the collector default and today the only value written.
list.label: Granularity
list.name: granularity

list.description: The common grid the two deviation legs are resampled onto, in seconds. Set it to the COARSER of the venue and anchor granularities. Aligning rather than equi-joining on the raw bucket is what keeps the panel populated when the two feeds run at different rates, which they are expected to.
list.label: Basis alignment (s)
list.name: align_secs

list.description: Wall clock the hour-of-day profile is expressed in. UTC is neutral and right for comparing across currencies; pick a centre's own zone to read the profile as a local trading day. The weekday/weekend split is always computed on the New York FX week regardless of this setting.
list.label: Hour timezone
list.name: hour_tz
